Rebuild the decision around a supported patient-specific treatment or response constraint so that interpreting persistent potassium elevation and deciding substrate support each changes the chosen plan. Re-solve all alternatives after the edit; do not create a new threshold.

title: Persistent alkalosis after gastric drainage ends
fairness: The pH, PCO2 and bicarbonate are internally consistent with metabolic alkalosis. Low pretreatment urine chloride despite higher urine sodium supports a chloride-depleted maintaining process after the initiating gastric loss ends. Sodium chloride replacement with continued potassium chloride is the best offered addition.

The resident must distinguish the maintaining physiology from the ended loss and from an inference based on urine sodium, then select replacement instead of pharmacologic bicarbonate loss or mineralocorticoid blockade. Acetazolamide is particularly unattractive with current hypokalaemia, while spironolactone does not address the demonstrated chloride-depletion pattern. These are recognizable neighboring management errors.

The no-fluid/no-diuretic sampling context and absence of oedema are relevant to interpreting urine chloride and choosing replacement, not gratuitous feasibility permissions. The choices have different routes but comparable specificity and all answer the addition-to-potassium task. The classic mechanism remains high-yield and moderately difficult, rather than a hard stretch item.
The standalone historical reassessment is coherent. No confident clinical inaccuracy, unique wording-match shortcut or preceding-feedback dependence was identified.
